prompt:
A photograph of one paper page lying on a foundry statistician's desk at month end: the signed, filed copy of the monthly output return that the plant sends to the statistics bureau.

Across the head of the page runs the reporting rule, word for word:
'A WORKSHOP THAT HAS NOT REPORTED IS LEFT EMPTY. A ZERO, AN N/A OR A DASH IS A REPORTED FIGURE OF NIL AND MAKES THIS A FALSE RETURN.'

The body of the page is a table. Down the left edge are four part names, one per row. Across the top are four workshop columns headed SHOP 1, SHOP 2, SHOP 3, SHOP 4, and then a TOTAL column. These are the four part names and the month totals that stand in the TOTAL column:
AXLE ... 5020
CLUTCH ... 7240
DRUM ... 3660
SHAFT ... 2905

Down the right edge of the same page runs a narrow extract from the dispatch ledger, headed 'OUTPUT OF THE WORKSHOP THAT DID NOT REPORT', carrying one figure against each part row:
AXLE ... 840
CLUTCH ... 1290
DRUM ... 515
SHAFT ... 460

The statistician has already entered the return and signed it. In every one of the four rows, one workshop and one workshop only failed to report this month. An inspector ties the page out row by row: whatever stands in that row's workshop columns, together with that row's ledger figure, has to come to that row's month total. Work each row out for yourself -- I am deliberately not telling you which workshop column is the one that did not report in any row, and I am not telling you any of the workshop figures.

Nothing else may be written on the page: no arithmetic, no working, no note, and none of the words BLANK, MISSING, NIL or SAME anywhere. The only text on the page is the rule at the head, the row and column headings, the TOTAL column, the ledger extract and the figures the statistician entered.

The rule at the head, all four rows with their four workshop columns, the TOTAL column and the ledger extract must all be in the same picture, and every figure must be large and easy to read.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is filled in. Does this picture show one paper page carrying a printed table with part names down the left, several workshop columns, a total column, and a narrow strip of figures down the right edge? A photo, a scan or a plain rendering all count as yes. Answer no only if it shows something unrelated, or a bare sheet with an answer written on it. Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: one part row of the printed output return

steps.read_crop: Copy the part name printed at the left-hand end of this cut-out. Write the name and nothing else.

Copy the four workshop figures printed across the middle of this cut-out from left to right, separated by commas, putting the word EMPTY in place of any one of the four that has nothing printed in it. Write nothing else.
